title: 10-Day Northeast India Itinerary: Meghalaya · Kaziranga · Tawang · The Seven Sisters
description: From the living root bridges of Meghalaya to the one-horned rhinos of Kaziranga to the ancient Tawang Monastery at 10,000 feet — this is India's wildest, most unexplored frontier. Ten days through Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, and Meghalaya.

days.title: Gateway to the Northeast
days.description: Arrive in Guwahati, Assam's largest city and the gateway to the entire Northeast. Ease into the region with ancient temples and a river cruise.

activities.name: Arrive at Guwahati Airport (GAU)
activities.description: Fly into Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport. Your hired car and driver should be waiting — arrange through your hotel or a local agency in advance. One of India's most important Shakti Peethas, this ancient Hindu temple sits atop Nilachal Hill with panoramic views of Guwahati. The temple's unique architecture and spiritual energy are powerful even for non-religious visitors.

activities.name: Umananda Island
activities.description: Take a short ferry ride across the Brahmaputra to this tiny river island — one of the world's smallest inhabited islands, home to a Shiva temple and golden langur monkeys.

activities.name: Brahmaputra River Sunset Cruise
activities.description: Board the Alfresco Grand or one of the smaller boats for a sunset cruise on the mighty Brahmaputra. Watch the city light up as the river turns golden — this is the best way to grasp the scale of Asia's widest river.

days.neighborhoods: Kaziranga National Park · Jeep Safari · Tea Gardens
days.title: Rhino Country
days.description: Drive east to Kaziranga National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinoceros population.

activities.name: Drive Guwahati → Kaziranga (4-5 hours)
activities.description: Head east on NH-37 through lush green Assam countryside. Stop at roadside tea stalls — Assam produces more tea than anywhere else in India. The road passes through sprawling tea estates with stunning views.

activities.name: Kaziranga Central Range Jeep Safari
activities.description: Book the afternoon jeep safari through the Central Range (Kohora) — the most popular zone with the highest rhino density. You'll almost certainly see one-horned rhinos, wild water buffalo, and possibly elephants from your open-top jeep.

activities.name: Kaziranga Orchid Park & Local Market
activities.description: Visit the orchid and biodiversity park near Kohora gate to see dozens of native orchid species. Then explore the small Kohora market for local handicrafts and bamboo products.

days.title: Into Arunachal Pradesh
days.description: Early morning elephant safari, then begin the drive into Arunachal Pradesh — climbing from the plains into the Himalayas through the ILP checkpoint at Bhalukpong.

activities.name: Kaziranga Elephant Safari (Optional)
activities.description: The 5:30 AM elephant safari lets you ride through the tall grasslands at eye-level with rhinos. An unforgettable experience — elephants can navigate terrain jeeps can't reach, bringing you incredibly close to wildlife.

activities.name: Drive Kaziranga → Bomdila (7-8 hours)
activities.description: The long drive climbs from Assam's plains through Tezpur, past the Bhalukpong checkpoint (have your ILP ready), and winds up into the mountains to Bomdila at 8,500 ft. The landscape transformation is dramatic — from tea gardens to dense subtropical forest to alpine terrain.

activities.name: Bomdila Monasteries
activities.description: Explore the Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling Monastery (Upper Gompa) and the Lower Gompa. These Tibetan Buddhist monasteries feature stunning wall paintings, prayer wheels, and views of the Himalayan foothills. The monks are welcoming and you may observe evening prayer chanting.

days.neighborhoods: Bomdila · Sela Pass · Jaswant Garh · Nuranang Falls · Tawang
days.title: The Road to Tawang
days.description: One of the most spectacular drives in the world — crossing Sela Pass at 13,700 ft with frozen lakes and snow-capped peaks, through the Tawang Valley to the ancient monastery town.

activities.name: Drive Bomdila → Tawang via Sela Pass (7-8 hours)
activities.description: Leave early. The drive crosses the legendary Sela Pass at 13,700 ft — often snow-covered even in April. The frozen Sela Lake glitters below the road. This is one of the highest motorable passes in India and the views are otherworldly.

activities.name: Jaswant Garh War Memorial
activities.description: Stop at this memorial honoring Jaswant Singh Rawat, a soldier who single-handedly held off Chinese forces in 1962. The Indian Army maintains the memorial — soldiers here tell the story with genuine emotion. One of India's most moving war memorials. A spectacular 100-meter waterfall cascading down mossy cliffs in a dense forest gorge. The short hike down to the base is steep but rewarding. Known locally as 'the heart of Tawang.'

activities.name: Arrive in Tawang
activities.description: Check into your hotel and rest. Tawang sits at 10,000 ft — you may feel the altitude. Take it easy tonight. Walk through the small town center if you have energy — the views of the valley and monastery are stunning at sunset.

days.neighborhoods: Tawang Monastery · Madhuri Lake · Buddha Park
days.title: Tawang — Monastery & Sacred Lakes
days.description: A full day exploring Tawang — the spiritual heart of Arunachal Pradesh and home to the world's second-largest Buddhist monastery after Lhasa's Potala Palace.

activities.name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
activities.description: Founded in 1680, this is the world's second-largest Buddhist monastery and the largest in India. The three-story main prayer hall houses a massive gilded Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and centuries of Tibetan Buddhist heritage. The 6th Dalai Lama was born here.

activities.name: Sangestar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
activities.description: A hauntingly beautiful lake formed by an earthquake in 1950, surrounded by dead tree stumps rising from turquoise water and backed by snow-capped peaks. Named after a Bollywood film shot here, but far more stunning than any movie. A beautifully maintained memorial to soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. The evening sound and light show is deeply moving — told by an army of ghosts who narrate the battle.

activities.name: Buddha Park (Gorsam Chorten)
activities.description: A striking 40-foot illuminated Buddha statue surrounded by smaller chortens and prayer flags. Visit at dusk when it's lit up against the mountain backdrop. The adjacent garden is perfect for a peaceful evening stroll.

days.title: Return Through the Mountains
days.description: Begin the journey back south through Arunachal's stunning valleys. Stop in Dirang — a beautiful Himalayan valley with its own monasteries, hot springs, and the serene Sangti Valley.

activities.name: Drive Tawang → Dirang (5-6 hours)
activities.description: Retrace the spectacular Sela Pass route but this time heading downhill with different light and perspectives. Stop again at viewpoints you missed on the way up. The descent into the Kameng River valley is stunning.

activities.name: Dirang Dzong (Fortress)
activities.description: A 500-year-old stone fortress perched on a hilltop above the town. Still partially inhabited by Monpa families, it's one of the most atmospheric historical sites in Arunachal — crumbling stone walls, prayer flags, and sweeping valley views. A hidden valley just 15 km from Dirang — incredibly peaceful with the Sangti River winding through it, surrounded by kiwi orchards and mountain meadows. In winter, endangered black-necked cranes visit. In April, it's lush and green.

activities.name: Hot Springs & Rest
activities.description: Soak in Dirang's natural hot springs by the river. The sulfuric water is said to have healing properties. After days in Tawang, this is the perfect reset before heading to Meghalaya.

days.title: Into Meghalaya — the Abode of Clouds
days.description: Long drive day from Arunachal back through Guwahati and up to Shillong, Meghalaya's capital — the Scotland of the East with its rolling hills, pine forests, and colonial-era charm.

activities.name: Drive Dirang → Guwahati → Shillong (10-12 hours)
activities.description: This is the longest drive of the trip. Leave very early (5-6 AM). Drop through Arunachal's foothills back to Guwahati, then climb south into the Khasi Hills to Shillong at 4,900 ft. The landscape shifts from Himalayan alpine to rolling green hills reminiscent of Scotland.

activities.name: Arrive in Shillong
activities.description: Check into your hotel in Shillong's Police Bazar area — the city center with restaurants, shops, and cafes. Shillong has a surprisingly cosmopolitan vibe with live music venues, coffee shops, and a strong indie rock scene (it's called India's Rock Capital).

days.neighborhoods: Cherrapunji · Nongriat · Living Root Bridges · Nohkalikai Falls
days.title: Living Root Bridges & Waterfalls
days.description: The highlight of Meghalaya — trek down to the legendary double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat and witness the world's most powerful waterfall at Nohkalikai.

activities.name: Drive Shillong → Tyrna Village (2.5 hours)
activities.description: Leave by 6 AM for Tyrna, the trailhead for the Nongriat living root bridges. The drive passes through Sohra (Cherrapunji) — one of the wettest places on Earth — with spectacular canyon views along the way.

activities.name: Trek to Nongriat Double-Decker Living Root Bridge
activities.description: The living root bridges of Meghalaya are one of the most extraordinary human-nature collaborations on Earth. The Khasi people train the aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees across rivers, creating bridges that strengthen over centuries. The double-decker bridge at Nongriat — two bridges stacked on top of each other — is the crown jewel. The trek is 3,500 stone steps each way through dense tropical forest.

activities.name: Nohkalikai Falls
activities.description: At 1,115 feet, this is India's tallest plunge waterfall — water cascading off a cliff into a turquoise pool far below. The viewpoint is easily accessible by car from the main road, no hiking required. In April with pre-monsoon rains starting, the falls should have good flow.

activities.name: Stay in Cherrapunji (Sohra)
activities.description: Check into a guesthouse in Sohra and collapse after the trek. Many have cliff-edge views over the Bangladesh plains far below. On clear evenings, you can see the flatlands stretching to the horizon.

days.neighborhoods: Dawki · Umngot River · Mawlynnong · Bangladesh Border
days.title: Crystal River & Asia's Cleanest Village
days.description: From the wettest place on Earth to crystal-clear waters and the cleanest village in Asia — today showcases Meghalaya's incredible diversity.

activities.name: Drive Cherrapunji → Dawki (2-3 hours)
activities.description: Wind through misty Khasi Hills down to the Indo-Bangladesh border at Dawki. The road itself is a scenic journey through dense forest and small Khasi villages. The Umngot River at Dawki is famous for water so crystal-clear that boats appear to float in mid-air. Take a wooden boat ride upstream — the riverbed is visible 15-20 feet below through glass-like water. This is the photo that launched Meghalaya onto every travel Instagram.

activities.name: Mawlynnong Village — Asia's Cleanest
activities.description: This tiny Khasi village won the title of Cleanest Village in Asia and maintains its reputation with community-driven cleanliness. Bamboo dustbins line every path, flower gardens bloom outside every home, and the entire village is spotlessly maintained. Visit the living root bridge nearby and the sky walk bamboo platform. Near Mawlynnong, a viewpoint lets you gaze across the border into the endless flat plains of Bangladesh — a dramatic contrast to the hills you're standing on. The border between India's Northeast and Bangladesh is one of the most visually striking in the world.

activities.name: Return to Shillong
activities.description: Drive back to Shillong (3-4 hours) for your final night in Meghalaya. Use the evening to explore anything you missed — Don Bosco Museum (Northeast India's tribal cultures), or simply enjoy the Police Bazar atmosphere.

days.title: Farewell to the Seven Sisters
days.description: A gentle final day — Shillong's last sights, the stunning Umiam Lake, and a relaxed drive to Guwahati for your departure flight.

activities.name: Shillong Morning Walk — Laitumkhrah & Cathedral
activities.description: Take a morning walk through Laitumkhrah neighborhood — Shillong's trendiest area with independent coffee shops, bookstores, and street art. Visit the Cathedral of Mary Help of Christians, one of Northeast India's most beautiful churches. If you didn't visit yesterday, spend the morning here. Seven floors dedicated to Northeast India's 200+ tribal communities — their art, music, textiles, weapons, and beliefs. One of the best ethnographic museums in all of India.

activities.name: Umiam Lake
activities.description: Stop at Umiam Lake on the way to Guwahati — a massive reservoir surrounded by pine-covered hills. It looks like a lake in the Scottish Highlands. Kayaking and boating available, or just enjoy the view from the roadside. The final drive descends from the Khasi Hills back to the Brahmaputra plains. Give yourself plenty of buffer for your flight — the road can be slow with truck traffic near Guwahati.

activities.name: Depart from Guwahati
activities.description: Say goodbye to the Seven Sisters. Ten days is barely enough to scratch the surface — Nagaland's Hornbill Festival, Manipur's Loktak Lake, Sikkim's mountains, and Tripura's temples are all waiting for your return.
